dd.p: Displays exactly one row, selected using the same table and record identifiers as list. All columns are displayed, including _uuid, empty sets and maps, and default values. Output uses list-style column alignment.

By default, UUID references declared in the schema are displayed using the referenced row's nonempty name column, if present. Otherwise, the UUID is displayed. Other columns, including UUIDs that are not schema references, retain their usual database value representation. References in sets and maps retain their delimiters and key-value associations. This display is intended for inspection, not as input to database modification commands.

With --all, reference values remain UUIDs, and the full contents of referenced rows are displayed below the referring column, indented by four spaces per level. Peer rows are separated by blank lines and a dashed line. Both strong and weak forward references are followed, including references in map keys and values. Reverse references are not followed. A row already on the current expansion path is not expanded again, preventing cycles. A shared row can still be expanded under each of its referring rows.

A missing or ambiguous table or record is an error. The command requires list output with string data and headings; incompatible table formatting options are rejected. It does not change the behavior of show or list.
